As Mastercard (MA) Stock Value Rose, Toronto Dominion Bank Lifted Holding by $6.91 Million; As Facebook (FB) Valuation Declined, Holder Bank Pictet & Cie Asia LTD Has Cut by $1.41 Million Its Position
May 16, 2018 - By Richard Conner
Bank Pictet & Cie Asia Ltd decreased its stake in Facebook Inc (FB) by 24.62% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Bank Pictet & Cie Asia Ltd sold 8,036 shares as the company’s stock declined 14.10% with the market. The institutional investor held 24,610 shares of the technology company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $4.34M, down from 32,646 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Bank Pictet & Cie Asia Ltd who had been investing in Facebook Inc for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $529.72B market cap company. The stock decreased 0.72% or $1.3199 during the last trading session, reaching $183.0001. About 6.05 million shares traded. Facebook, Inc. (NASDAQ:FB) has risen 8.48% since May 16, 2017 and is uptrending. It has underperformed by 3.07% the S&P500.
Toronto Dominion Bank increased its stake in Mastercard Inc (MA) by 12.31% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Toronto Dominion Bank bought 45,736 shares as the company’s stock rose 14.37% while stock markets declined. The institutional investor held 417,271 shares of the business services company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $63.16 million, up from 371,535 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Toronto Dominion Bank who had been investing in Mastercard Inc for a number of months, seems to be bullish on the $200.54B market cap company. The stock increased 0.05% or $0.1 during the last trading session, reaching $192.1. About 714,924 shares traded. Mastercard Incorporated (NYSE:MA) has risen 54.12% since May 16, 2017 and is uptrending. It has outperformed by 42.57% the S&P500.
Analysts await Facebook, Inc. (NASDAQ:FB) to report earnings on July, 25. They expect $1.72 EPS, up 30.30% or $0.40 from last year’s $1.32 per share. FB’s profit will be $4.98 billion for 26.60 P/E if the $1.72 EPS becomes a reality. After $1.69 actual EPS reported by Facebook, Inc. for the previous quarter, Wall Street now forecasts 1.78% EPS growth.
